title: The Missing Confession
premise: Estate lawyer Mirabel Hartwell is summoned to read the will of Edmund Voss, founder of the town of Grayhollow — only to discover a second, contradictory will dated thirty years after Voss's official death. When investigators exhume Voss's coffin and find it empty, Mirabel realizes the town's founding legend is a fabrication sustained by a circle of families who inherited everything on a lie. Following threads through forged alibis and a vanished witness named June Okafor, Mirabel uncovers that Voss faked his death to escape prosecution for a fatal fire, lived out his years nearby, and entrusted the true confession to June — who has been hiding in plain sight as the town archivist. In the climax, the conspirators' last living member tries to destroy the confession and silence June; Mirabel chooses justice over the law, publishing the confession and letting the inheritance collapse, then takes June and her chosen family into his own found household.
about_author: August Dravenmoor spent a decade as a small-town court clerk before turning to fiction, giving his mysteries an insider's feel for probate law and civic mythology. He writes from a converted schoolhouse in rural New England, where he collects antique wills and local legends.

chapters.title: The Second Will
chapters.summary: Mirabel Hartwell's POV. Called to Grayhollow to read Edmund Voss's will, Mirabel finds two documents: the public testament and a sealed one dated decades later, naming an unknown beneficiary. The family demands he destroy it; his pride in closing every case makes him refuse. Emotional beat: professional curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Empty Oak
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The exhumation order comes through, and the coffin is opened before the whole town: no body, only river stones and a rotted ledger page. Grief turns to fury among the founding families. Mirabel notices someone in the crowd watching him with recognition rather than shock. Emotional beat: vertigo — the ground truth itself has shifted.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, with archival excerpts. He reconstructs the night Voss supposedly drowned: five witnesses, five matching statements, all signed at the same notary within an hour. Too perfect. A threatening note appears in his car. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt shadowed by first real fear.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Drawer
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Tracing the ledger page leads to the town archive and its quiet keeper, June Okafor, who deflects him expertly — but a locked drawer bears initials that match the second will's beneficiary. That night the archive suffers a small fire. Emotional beat: attraction and suspicion entwined; guilt over endangering her.

chapters.title: What the Fire Left
chapters.summary: June Okafor's POV. June reveals she was a child in the house fire Voss was fleeing when he 'died' — the fire that killed her mother. She has guarded his written confession for thirty years, waiting for someone who couldn't be bought. Emotional beat: grief finally spoken aloud, trust extended like a held breath.

chapters.title: The Circle of Five
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Of the five alibi-witnesses, three are dead under mundane circumstances, one has dementia and babbles about 'the man in the boathouse,' and the last — Councilman Aldous Pike — is now Mirabel's most charming enemy. Pike offers Mirabel money, then veiled threats. Emotional beat: isolation; realizing the law itself is compromised.

chapters.title: Boathouse Bones
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Following the demented witness's fragment, Mirabel finds remains under the collapsed Voss boathouse — the real Edmund Voss, dead since roughly the year of the second will's date. Someone killed him for real, long ago, and let the legend stand. Emotional beat: horror reframing everything; the mystery deepens rather than resolves.

chapters.title: Confession and Counterfeit
chapters.summary: Alternating Mirabel and June POVs. The confession surfaces: Voss wrote it as penance, but the second will was forged by one of the Five to control the estate forever. Forensic details point to Pike's late father — and to Pike finishing the job. June agrees to testify. Emotional beat: clarity arriving just as danger peaks.

chapters.title: The Long Night in Grayhollow
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Pike, cornered, breaks into the archive to burn the confession and take June hostage. Mirabel arrives, talks him down using the dementia witness's corroboration and the bones' evidence, while June records Pike's confession on the archive's old dictaphone. Police arrive too late to matter. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: What We Inherit
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, epilogue months later. The estate is dissolved into restitution for the fire's survivors; the town reckons with its false founder. Mirabel, who never lost a case, loses this one deliberately — and gains something better: June, the surviving witnesses' descendants, and a new kind of family around his dinner table. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
